To find the proportionality factor $C$, we express the spatial derivative of the wavefunction $\psi$ in terms of the Madelung--Bohm velocities. Writing the wavefunction in polar form,
$$\psi(x) = \sqrt{\mathcal{P}(x)}\, e^{i S(x)/\hbar},$$
the spatial derivatives give:
$$\partial_\mu \psi = \left( \frac{\partial_\mu \mathcal{P}}{2\mathcal{P}} + \frac{i}{\hbar} \partial_\mu S \right) \psi.$$

The Madelung--Bohm current velocity $\pi_\mu$ and osmotic velocity $u_\mu$ are defined as:
$$\pi_\mu = \frac{1}{m}\partial_\mu S \implies \frac{1}{\hbar}\partial_\mu S = \frac{m}{\hbar}\pi_\mu,$$
$$u_\mu = \frac{\hbar}{2m}\frac{\partial_\mu \mathcal{P}}{\mathcal{P}} \implies \frac{\partial_\mu \mathcal{P}}{2\mathcal{P}} = \frac{m}{\hbar}u_\mu.$$

Substituting these expressions into $\partial_\mu \psi$ yields:
$$\partial_\mu \psi = \frac{m}{\hbar}(u_\mu + i\pi_\mu)\psi = i\frac{m}{\hbar}(\pi_\mu - i u_\mu)\psi = i\frac{m}{\hbar}\eta_\mu \psi,$$
where $\eta_\mu = \pi_\mu - i u_\mu$ is the complex velocity field.

The Fubini--Study metric on the projective Hilbert space of pure states is given by:
$$g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \operatorname{Re}\left[ \langle \partial_\mu \psi | \partial_\nu \psi \rangle - \langle \partial_\mu \psi | \psi \rangle \langle \psi | \partial_\nu \psi \rangle \right].$$

Projecting onto the subspace orthogonal to $|\psi\rangle$, we find:
$$\langle \partial_\mu \psi_\perp | \partial_\nu \psi_\perp \rangle = \frac{m^2}{\hbar^2} \operatorname{Cov}_{\mathcal{P}}(\eta_\mu^*, \eta_\nu).$$

Taking the real part using $\eta_\mu^* = \pi_\mu + i u_\mu$ and $\eta_\nu = \pi_\nu - i u_\nu$:
$$\operatorname{Re}[\eta_\mu^* \eta_\nu] = \pi_\mu \pi_\nu + u_\mu u_\nu,$$
which leads directly to:
$$g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{m^2}{\hbar^2} \bigl[\operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu, \pi_\nu) + \operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu, u_\nu)\bigr]_{\mathcal{P}}.$$

Replacing $\hbar$ with $x$, the proportionality factor is:
$$C = \frac{m^2}{x^2}.$$

ANSWER: m^2/x^2
